# Payments
## What is Payment?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/#what-is-payment "Direct link to What is Payment?")
Payments refer to the transfer of money, typically from a customer to a merchant, in exchange for goods or services. Payments can be made using various methods such as cash, credit or debit cards, mobile wallets, bank transfers, and online payment platforms. The process of making a payment involves the authorization and verification of the transaction, the transfer of funds, and the confirmation of successful payment completion. Payments are a fundamental aspect of commerce and financial transactions, enabling businesses to receive compensation for products or services rendered.
## Payment modes[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/#payment-modes "Direct link to Payment modes")
Payment modes refer to the methods or channels through which customers can pay for goods or services, encompassing both one-time payments and options to store payment information for future transactions. These payment methods play a crucial role in the payment operations of a business or e-commerce platform.
## CCG Offered Payment modes and transctions[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/#ccg-offered-payment-modes-and-transctions "Direct link to CCG Offered Payment modes and transctions")
  * [Payment Modes](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/payment-modes/)
  * Payment Transactions
    * [Pre-Authorization](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/pre-auth-transactions/)
    * [Sale Transacrions](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/sale-transactions/)
    * [Partial Authorization](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/pre-auth-transactions/partial-authorization/)


## Agent assisted payments[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/#agent-assisted-payments "Direct link to Agent assisted payments")
Agent-assisted payments refer to transactions where a human agent, such as a customer service representative or cashier, helps facilitate the payment process on behalf of the customer. This type of payment method involves direct interaction with a live agent to complete the payment, as opposed to fully automated or self-service transactions.
CCG offers agent assisted payments through various channels including `IVR` and agent assisted payments can be completed through CCG Widget and CCG API
### IVR Payment[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/#ivr-payment "Direct link to IVR Payment")
CCG provides a payment API with PCI scope that allows agents to securely process customer transactions via IVR.
  * When the customer is not found, a new customer will be created, a payment method will be generated and saved upon request, and the payment will be processed accordingly.
  * If the customer is located, a payment method will be generated and saved upon request, and the payment will be processed accordingly.




# ACH
## Overview[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#overview "Direct link to Overview")
ACH (Automated Clearing House) is an electronic network for financial transactions in the United States. ACH payments are electronic payments made through the Automated Clearing House network, which processes large volumes of credit and debit transactions in batches.
## How ACH Payments Work[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#how-ach-payments-work "Direct link to How ACH Payments Work")
ACH Payment Process
  1. **Initiation** : The customer provides bank account details and authorization
  2. **Processing** : The payment is submitted to the ACH network
  3. **Settlement** : Funds are transferred between financial institutions
  4. **Posting** : The transaction is completed and recorded in both accounts


ACH payments typically take 1-3 business days to process and settle.
## Types of ACH Transactions[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#types-of-ach-transactions "Direct link to Types of ACH Transactions")
  * **Direct Deposit** : Payroll, tax refunds, and other deposits
  * **Direct Payment** : Bill payments, subscription payments, and one-time purchases
  * **B2B Payments** : Business-to-business transactions
  * **P2P Transfers** : Person-to-person money transfers


## Benefits of ACH Payments[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#benefits-of-ach-payments "Direct link to Benefits of ACH Payments")
Benefit | Description  
---|---  
Cost-Effective | Lower processing fees compared to credit cards (typically $0.20-$1.50 per transaction)  
Reliable | Established, secure network with strong regulatory oversight  
Convenient | Enables recurring payments and automated transactions  
Eco-Friendly | Reduces paper usage compared to checks  
## Key Considerations[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#key-considerations "Direct link to Key Considerations")
  * **Return Rates** : Managing ACH returns (NSF, invalid account, etc.)
  * **Risk Management** : Fraud prevention and transaction monitoring
  * **Timing** : Understanding settlement timeframes
  * **Compliance** : Following NACHA rules and regulations
  * **Customer Experience** : Proper communication about timing and authorization


## ACH in Convenient Checkout[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#ach-in-convenient-checkout "Direct link to ACH in Convenient Checkout")
The Convenient Checkout platform supports ACH payments with the following features:
  * **Multiple Entry Methods** : Support for bank account details entry via:
    * Direct input of routing and account numbers
    * Stored payment methods (wallet)
    * IVR (Interactive Voice Response) systems
  * **Consent Management** : Robust framework for capturing and storing customer consent
    * Web-based consent collection
    * Telephonic consent collection
    * Paper-based consent handling
  * **Payment Flows** :
    * One-time payments
    * Pay and Store
    * Payment with stored bank accounts


## Security and Compliance[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#security-and-compliance "Direct link to Security and Compliance")
Security Requirements
ACH payments require strict security measures:
  * **Data Encryption** : All bank account information must be encrypted at rest and in transit
  * **PCI Compliance** : While not credit card data, bank information requires similar protection
  * **Access Controls** : Strict limitations on who can view full account details
  * **Data Retention** : Policies for secure storage and deletion of sensitive data


NACHA Compliance
All ACH transactions must comply with NACHA (National Automated Clearing House Association) rules:
  * **Authorization** : Proper customer consent must be obtained and documented
  * **Authentication** : Identity verification of the account holder
  * **Format Requirements** : Transactions must adhere to NACHA file specifications
  * **Return Thresholds** : Merchants must maintain acceptable return rates
  * **Record Retention** : Authorization records must be kept for at least 2 years


## Related Documentation[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/#related-documentation "Direct link to Related Documentation")
  * **[ACH Consent Requirements](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/)**




# Replaced Payment Method
Quick Reference
  * **Purpose:** Explains how CCG handles replacement of payment methods (e.g., expired cards).
  * **Key Actions:** Duplicate card removal, merchant notifications, and event structure.
  * **Triggers:** Card expiration, reissued cards, bank account updates, wallet merge.
  * **Supported Types:** `CARD` and `BANK ACCOUNT`
  * **Use:** Reference for event flows and merchant integration.


* * *
## Scenario Overview[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#scenario-overview "Direct link to Scenario Overview")
Suppose a user has card **A** (ending 1234) in their wallet. When card **A** expires and the user receives a new card **B** (ending 5678), they add card **B** to their wallet. CCG receives an event from the vendor indicating that card **A** has been updated to card **B**.
  * Card **A** is treated as a duplicate and replaced by card **B** in the user's wallet.
  * This logic applies to all supported payment method types (e.g., cards, bank accounts, digital wallets).


### Common Replacement Triggers[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#common-replacement-triggers "Direct link to Common Replacement Triggers")
  * **Card Expiration** : When a card reaches its expiry date and a new one is issued.
  * **Lost or Stolen Cards** : When a card needs to be reissued due to loss or theft.
  * **Bank Changes** : When a bank account changes routing or account numbers.
  * **Card Network Updates** : When payment networks update card numbers for security reasons.


* * *
## What Happens to the Duplicate Card?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#what-happens-to-the-duplicate-card "Direct link to What Happens to the Duplicate Card?")
  * CCG automatically removes the duplicate card **A** from the wallet.
  * Merchants are notified via a [`PAYMENT_METHOD_DELETED`](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/v1/developers/add-on-services/webhooks/payment-methods/) event.
  * All associated payment links to the old payment method are updated to reference the new payment method.


* * *
## How Are Merchants Notified of the Replacement?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#how-are-merchants-notified-of-the-replacement "Direct link to How Are Merchants Notified of the Replacement?")
  * CCG sends a [`PAYMENT_METHOD_REPLACED`](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/v1/developers/add-on-services/webhooks/payment-methods/) event.
  * This event includes details of the new payment method (**B**) and the replaced (deleted) payment method (**A**).
  * Merchants can use this information to update their records and maintain accurate payment method data.


### Implementation Considerations for Merchants[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#implementation-considerations-for-merchants "Direct link to Implementation Considerations for Merchants")
  * If your system stores references to card **A** , those should be updated to card **B**.
  * Update any recurring payments or saved payment instructions to use the new payment method ID.
  * Validate that the event was processed successfully to maintain data consistency.


* * *
## Sample Event Structure[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#sample-event-structure "Direct link to Sample Event Structure")
**PAYMENT_METHOD_REPLACED EVENT**
```
{  
  "name": "PAYMENT_METHOD_REPLACED",  
  "payload": {  
    "paymentMethod": { // Payment Method information of CARD B   
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",  
      "card": {  
        "last4": "5678",  
        "type": "CARD",  
        "status": "ACTIVE",  
        "cardBrand": "VISA",  
        "expiryYear": 2028,  
        "nameOnCard": "John Doe",  
        "expiryMonth": 12,  
        "zipCode": "12345",  
        "manufacturerCard": false  
      },  
      "paymentMethodDetails": {  
        "last4": "5678",  
        "type": "CARD",  
        "status": "ACTIVE",  
        "cardBrand": "VISA",  
        "expiryYear": 2028,  
        "nameOnCard": "John Doe",  
        "expiryMonth": 12,  
        "zipCode": "12345",  
        "manufacturerCard": false  
      },  
      "default": true,  
      "paymentMethodType": "CARD",  
      "nickname": "Personal Card"  
    },  
    "customer": {  
      "enterpriseId": "enterprise id",  
      "hsid": "hsid",  
      "dateOfBirth": "YYYY-MM-DD",  
      "metadata": {  
        "patientId": "rx-patient-id"  
      }  
    },  
    "agent": {  
      "firstName": "First Name",  
      "lastName": "Last Name",  
      "userId": "msId",  
      "isAccessVerified": true  
    },  
    "deletedPaymentMethodId": "597f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f12" // CCG Payment Method ID of CARD A   
  }  
}  

```

* * *
## Benefits of Automatic Payment Method Replacement[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#benefits-of-automatic-payment-method-replacement "Direct link to Benefits of Automatic Payment Method Replacement")
  * **Reduced Payment Failures** : Fewer declined transactions due to expired or outdated payment methods.
  * **Enhanced Customer Experience** : Users don't need to manually update payment information across all merchants.
  * **Operational Efficiency** : Merchants automatically receive updated payment method details.
  * **Consistent Data** : All systems maintain synchronized and up-to-date payment information.


* * *
## Frequently Asked Questions[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#frequently-asked-questions "Direct link to Frequently Asked Questions")
### What happens to subscriptions that use the replaced payment method?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#what-happens-to-subscriptions-that-use-the-replaced-payment-method "Direct link to What happens to subscriptions that use the replaced payment method?")
Subscriptions and recurring payments using the old payment method will automatically use the new payment method, provided merchants have implemented proper handling of the `PAYMENT_METHOD_REPLACED` event.
### Can users opt-out of automatic payment method replacement?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#can-users-opt-out-of-automatic-payment-method-replacement "Direct link to Can users opt-out of automatic payment method replacement?")
No, this is a system-level feature that maintains wallet integrity and ensures payment methods remain current.
### How quickly does the replacement process occur?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#how-quickly-does-the-replacement-process-occur "Direct link to How quickly does the replacement process occur?")
The replacement process happens in near real-time once CCG receives the update event from the payment provider.
### What if a merchant misses the replacement event?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/replaced-payment-method/#what-if-a-merchant-misses-the-replacement-event "Direct link to What if a merchant misses the replacement event?")
Merchants should implement retry mechanisms and reconciliation processes to handle missed events. CCG's API also provides ways to verify current payment method status.
* * *
> **Note:** This event-driven approach ensures merchants always have the latest payment method information and can provide a seamless experience to their customers.


# 3D Secure Authentication
### What is 3D Secure Authentication?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#what-is-3d-secure-authentication "Direct link to What is 3D Secure Authentication?")
**3DS (3D Secure)** is a security protocol that adds an extra layer of authentication for online credit and debit card transactions. When a card is enrolled in 3DS, the cardholder may be asked to enter a password or a one-time code to verify their identity during checkout. This process helps prevent unauthorized use of the card online.
**Common 3DS authentication brands:**
  * **Verified by Visa** (Visa)
  * **Mastercard SecureCode** (Mastercard)
  * **American Express SafeKey** (American Express)


**Benefits of 3DS:**
  * Enhanced security for online transactions
  * Reduced risk of fraud for both merchants and cardholders
  * Increased trust in digital payments


> 3DS authentication is typically triggered during online purchases, providing real-time protection against fraudulent activity.
## Business Rules[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#business-rules "Direct link to Business Rules")
  * **Adding 3DS enabled card**
    * Only [**Authenticated Users**](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/users/#users) are permitted to add cards that require 3D Secure (3DS) authentication. [Learn more](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#agent-cannot-add-a-card-that-requires-3ds-challenge)
  * **Payment with 3DS auth card**
    * Both [**Agents**](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/users/#users) and **Authenticated Users** are allowed to make payments using cards that have **already been authenticated** and stored in the wallet
    * Only **Authenticated User** can pay with 3DS cards that requires 3D Secure (3DS) authentication for every transaction


## Business Use Case[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#business-use-case "Direct link to Business Use Case")

## Special Use-Case[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#special-use-case "Direct link to Special Use-Case")
### 3DS-enabled card cannot be designated as a manufacturer card[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#3ds-enabled-card-cannot-be-designated-as-a-manufacturer-card "Direct link to 3DS-enabled card cannot be designated as a manufacturer card")
3DS emphasizes consumer-level identity verification (e.g., OTP, SMS verification, biometrics, authentication via issuer’s banking portal). Manufacturer Cards often represent corporate-level or supplier-level accounts, which typically have transaction management and approval workflows rather than individual cardholder authentication. These corporate/wholesale cards may explicitly avoid or bypass 3DS-style purposes and are typically restricted from regular commerce flows.
Because of these fundamental differences in purpose, security requirements, and regulatory considerations, a 3DS-enabled card cannot serve as a manufacturer card.
### Agent cannot add a card that requires 3DS challenge[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#agent-cannot-add-a-card-that-requires-3ds-challenge "Direct link to Agent cannot add a card that requires 3DS challenge")
**Reasoning:**
  * 3DS authentication is designed to be completed only by the cardholder for security and regulatory compliance.
  * Agents are not authorized to perform 3DS challenges on behalf of users, as this would violate security protocols and potentially expose sensitive information.


**Alternate Paths:**
  * Agents can send a secure, time-limited link via SMS or email, allowing the authenticated user to add the card or make payment and complete the 3DS challenge themselves. For more information, Refer [TEXT](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-method-channels/text-channel/) and [EMAIL](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-method-channels/email-channel/) channels.




# Card Payments
## Overview[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#overview "Direct link to Overview")
Card payments are electronic transactions that use credit, debit, or prepaid cards to transfer funds from a cardholder's account to a merchant's account. The Convenient Checkout platform supports all major card types and provides a secure, compliant infrastructure for processing card payments across various channels and use cases.
Card Payment Networks
Our platform supports all major card networks:
  * **Visa** : The largest global payment network
  * **Mastercard** : Second-largest global payment network
  * **American Express** : Premium card network with higher processing fees but affluent customer base
  * **Discover** : Popular US-based payment network
  * **JCB** : Japanese Credit Bureau, popular in Asia
  * **Diners Club International** : Primarily used for travel and entertainment


## How Card Payments Work[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#how-card-payments-work "Direct link to How Card Payments Work")
Card payments involve multiple parties and a series of steps to securely process transactions:
Card Payment Flow
  1. **Authorization** :
     * Customer presents card information
     * Merchant sends authorization request to payment processor
     * Issuing bank approves or declines
     * Approval response returned to merchant
  2. **Authentication** (for online transactions):
     * 3D Secure verification may be required
     * Customer authentication through issuing bank
  3. **Capture** :
     * Merchant submits transaction for settlement
     * Funds are transferred from issuing bank to acquiring bank
  4. **Settlement** :
     * Funds are deposited into merchant account
     * Typically takes 1-3 business days
  5. **Reconciliation** :
     * Transaction data matched with bank deposits


## Card Payment Types[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#card-payment-types "Direct link to Card Payment Types")
Payment Type | Description | Use Cases  
---|---|---  
Credit Card | Revolving line of credit with deferred payment | Higher-value purchases, subscription billing  
Debit Card | Direct deduction from bank account | Everyday purchases, bill payments  
Prepaid Card | Pre-loaded with funds, no bank account needed | Gift cards, underbanked customers  
FSA/HSA Cards | Special purpose healthcare spending cards | Medical expenses, health services  
Virtual Cards | Card numbers generated for temporary use | One-time purchases, enhanced security  
## Card Processing Features[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#card-processing-features "Direct link to Card Processing Features")
The Convenient Checkout platform provides comprehensive card processing capabilities:
### Payment Entry Methods[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#payment-entry-methods "Direct link to Payment Entry Methods")
Card Entry Options
  * **Manual Entry** : Customer or agent manually enters card details
  * **Stored Cards** : Tokenized cards saved in the customer's wallet
  * **Card-Present** : In-person payments with physical cards (swipe, chip, tap)
  * **Digital Wallets** : Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay integration
  * **IVR Payments** : Card details collected through interactive voice response
  * **CSR-Assisted** : Customer service representative collects card data


### Transaction Types[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#transaction-types "Direct link to Transaction Types")
Supported Transaction Types
  * **Authorization** : Verifies card validity and available funds without capturing funds
  * **Capture** : Completes a previously authorized transaction
  * **Sale (Auth+Capture)** : Combined authorization and capture in a single step
  * **Refund** : Returns funds to the customer's card
  * **Void** : Cancels a transaction before settlement
  * **Verification** : Card validation without financial transaction


## Card Security Standards[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#card-security-standards "Direct link to Card Security Standards")
Card payments require adherence to strict security standards:
### PCI DSS Compliance[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#pci-dss-compliance "Direct link to PCI DSS Compliance")
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
PCI DSS is a set of security standards designed to ensure all companies that accept, process, store, or transmit credit card information maintain a secure environment. Key requirements include:
  1. **Network Security** : Install and maintain a firewall configuration
  2. **Data Protection** : Encrypt transmission of cardholder data
  3. **Vulnerability Management** : Regular system updates and security patches
  4. **Access Control** : Restrict access to cardholder data
  5. **Network Monitoring** : Regular testing of security systems
  6. **Security Policy** : Maintain a policy addressing information security


The Convenient Checkout platform is fully PCI DSS compliant, reducing merchant compliance burden.
### Tokenization[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#tokenization "Direct link to Tokenization")
Card Tokenization Process
Tokenization replaces sensitive card data with a unique identifier (token) that has no exploitable value. Benefits include:
  * **Reduced Risk** : Tokens cannot be used to conduct fraudulent transactions
  * **Simplified Compliance** : Reduces PCI DSS scope and requirements
  * **Enhanced Customer Experience** : Enables card storage for future use without security risks


Our platform handles tokenization automatically, securely storing customer payment methods for future use.
### 3D Secure (3DS)[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#3d-secure-3ds "Direct link to 3D Secure \(3DS\)")
Enhanced Authentication
3D Secure (including versions 1.0, 2.0, and 2.1) provides an additional security layer for online card transactions:
  * **Dynamic Authentication** : Risk-based approach that only challenges suspicious transactions
  * **Liability Shift** : Shifts fraud liability from merchant to issuing bank
  * **Reduced Cart Abandonment** : Newer versions (2.0+) offer frictionless flows for low-risk transactions


Our implementation supports the latest 3DS protocols while maintaining a smooth customer experience.
## Card Processing Implementation[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#card-processing-implementation "Direct link to Card Processing Implementation")
### Integration Options[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#integration-options "Direct link to Integration Options")
Integration Type | Description | Use Cases  
---|---|---

## Advanced Features[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#advanced-features "Direct link to Advanced Features")
### Recurring Payments[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#recurring-payments "Direct link to Recurring Payments")
Subscription and Recurring Billing
Convenient Checkout supports various recurring payment models:
  * **Fixed Recurring** : Same amount charged at regular intervals
  * **Variable Recurring** : Amount varies based on usage or billing
  * **Installment Plans** : Fixed number of payments over time
  * **Account Updater** : Automatically updates expired card information
  * **Retry Logic** : Configurable retry attempts for failed recurring payments


Recurring payments require explicit customer authorization and proper disclosure of terms.
### Multi-Currency Processing[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#multi-currency-processing "Direct link to Multi-Currency Processing")
International Payment Support
Process transactions in multiple currencies:
  * **Dynamic Currency Conversion** : Allow customers to pay in their local currency
  * **Multi-Currency Settlement** : Receive funds in preferred currency
  * **Exchange Rate Management** : Transparent exchange rate handling
  * **Regional Payment Methods** : Support for region-specific card types


### Card Verification and AVS[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#card-verification-and-avs "Direct link to Card Verification and AVS")
Fraud Prevention Measures
  * **Address Verification System (AVS)** : Compares billing address with issuing bank's records
  * **Card Verification Value (CVV/CVC)** : Validates the security code on the card
  * **Postal Code Verification** : Verifies the billing zip/postal code
  * **Velocity Checks** : Monitors transaction frequency for suspicious patterns
  * **Machine Learning Fraud Detection** : Advanced risk scoring algorithms


## Error Handling and Decline Management[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#error-handling-and-decline-management "Direct link to Error Handling and Decline Management")
### Common Decline Codes[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#common-decline-codes "Direct link to Common Decline Codes")
Understanding Decline Reasons
Decline Code | Description | Recommended Action  
---|---|---  
Insufficient Funds | Card lacks available funds | Suggest alternative payment method  
Card Expired | Card expiration date has passed | Request updated card information  
Invalid Card Number | Card number is incorrect | Verify card details  
Do Not Honor | Generic decline from issuing bank | Try alternative payment method  
AVS Mismatch | Address verification failed | Verify billing address  
CVV Mismatch | Security code verification failed | Verify security code  
Transaction Not Allowed | Card not enabled for this transaction type | Suggest alternative payment method  
Suspected Fraud | Transaction flagged as potentially fraudulent | Contact customer to verify transaction  
### Decline Recovery Strategies[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#decline-recovery-strategies "Direct link to Decline Recovery Strategies")
Optimizing Approval Rates
  * **Retry Logic** : Intelligent retry strategy for soft declines
  * **Account Updater** : Automatically refresh expired card details
  * **Decline Recycling** : Process declined transactions at optimal times
  * **Smart Routing** : Route transactions through different processors based on card type
  * **Alternative Payment Suggestions** : Offer different payment methods after decline


## Healthcare Industry Considerations[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/card/#healthcare-industry-considerations "Direct link to Healthcare Industry Considerations")
Healthcare-Specific Requirements
Card payments in healthcare have unique requirements:
  * **FSA/HSA Card Processing** : Support for qualified medical expenses
  * **HIPAA Compliance** : Secure handling of protected health information
  * **Eligibility Verification** : Integration with insurance eligibility APIs
  * **Payment Plans** : Flexible payment arrangements for large medical bills
  * **Patient Responsibility Calculator** : Estimating patient payment portion




# ACH Consent
## What is ACH Consent?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#what-is-ach-consent "Direct link to What is ACH Consent?")
ACH (Automated Clearing House) consent is a legal authorization provided by a customer that permits electronic debits from their bank account. This consent is required by NACHA (National Automated Clearing House Association) regulations before initiating any ACH transaction.
## When is Consent Required?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#when-is-consent-required "Direct link to When is Consent Required?")
Consent is **mandatory** for all ACH payments involving:
  * Saved payment methods (walletpaymentmethodId)
  * One-time payments without storing the payment method
  * IVR (Interactive Voice Response) payments
  * Any payment transaction using a Bank Account as the payment method


**Important** : Without valid consent, any payment transaction using a Bank Account payment method cannot and should not be processed.
## Consent Requirements by Payment Type[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#consent-requirements-by-payment-type "Direct link to Consent Requirements by Payment Type")
Payment Type | Consent Required | Notes  
---|---|---  
Bank Account (ACH) | Yes | Full consent object required  
Credit/Debit Card | No | Consent not required for card payments  
Saved Bank Account | Yes | Consent must be associated with stored payment method  
IVR Bank Account | Yes | Specific TEL consent type required  
### Consent Object Structure[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#consent-object-structure "Direct link to Consent Object Structure")
Show Consent Object JSON Schema
```
"consent": {  
  "merchantConsentId": "string",  
  "merchantConsentText": "string",  
  "collectionTimestamp": "string",  
  "collectionDetails": {  
    "type": "WEB",  
    "web": {  
      "ipAddress": "string",  
      "userAgent": "string"  
    },  
    "tel": {  
      "inboundPhoneNumber": {  
        "countryCode": "string",  
        "number": "string"  
      }  
    }  
  }  
}  

```

### Key Components:[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#key-components "Direct link to Key Components:")
  * **merchantConsentText** : The actual text of the consent agreement shown to the customer.
    * Example: "I authorize [Company Name] to electronically debit my account for the amount due."
  * **merchantConsentId** : A unique identifier that references a consent agreement stored by the merchant.
    * **Note** : merchantConsentText and merchantConsentId are mutually exclusive. The API prioritizes merchantConsentId since the primary responsibility for consent collection rests with the merchant.
  * **collectionTimestamp** : The timestamp indicating precisely when consent was collected from the customer.
    * Must be in ISO-8601 format (e.g., "2025-07-21T14:30:00Z")
  * **collectionDetails** : Contains information about how the consent was collected
    * **type** : Specifies the consent collection method (WEB, TEL, PPD)
    * **web** : Web-specific collection details (required when type is WEB)
    * **tel** : Telephonic collection details (required when type is TEL)


### NACHA-Compliant Consent Collection Types[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#nacha-compliant-consent-collection-types "Direct link to NACHA-Compliant Consent Collection Types")
NACHA regulations require specific consent collection methods for different ACH transaction types. The following types are specified in the `collectionDetails.type` field and are mutually exclusive:
#### 1. **WEB** - Online/Digital Consent[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#1-web---onlinedigital-consent "Direct link to 1-web---onlinedigital-consent")
  * **Definition** : Consent collected electronically via website or mobile application
  * **Required Fields** :
    * `collectionDetails.web.ipAddress`: Customer's IP address at time of consent
    * `collectionDetails.web.userAgent`: Browser/device information at time of consent
  * **Use Cases** : Self-service payments, online bill pay, recurring payment setup
  * **Example** : Customer agrees to ACH terms by checking a box on the payment page


#### 2. **TEL** - Telephonic Consent[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#2-tel---telephonic-consent "Direct link to 2-tel---telephonic-consent")
  * **Definition** : Verbal consent provided over the phone
  * **Required Fields** :
    * `collectionDetails.tel.inboundPhoneNumber`: Contains country code and phone number
  * **Use Cases** :
    * IVR (Interactive Voice Response) payments
    * Agent-assisted payments where customer is on the call
  * **Best Practice** : While not mandatory, recording the call reference ID is recommended


#### 3. **PPD** - Physical/Paper Consent[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#3-ppd---physicalpaper-consent "Direct link to 3-ppd---physicalpaper-consent")
  * **Definition** : Consent collected via physical signed document
  * **Required Components** :
    * `collectionDetails.ppd`: Contains information about the paper document and processing agent
  * **Use Case** : Customer provides a signed paper authorization form


### Validation and Error Handling[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#validation-and-error-handling "Direct link to Validation and Error Handling")
The payment processing system enforces strict consent validation:
  1. **Mandatory Requirement** : No ACH payment can proceed without a valid consent object
  2. **Validation Logic** :
     * Either `merchantConsentText` or `merchantConsentId` must be present (mutually exclusive)
     * `collectionTimestamp` must be included and must be a valid ISO-8601 timestamp
     * `collectionDetails.type` must be one of the supported values (WEB, TEL, PPD)
     * Type-specific fields must be present:
       * For WEB: `collectionDetails.web.ipAddress` and `collectionDetails.web.userAgent`
       * For TEL: `collectionDetails.tel.inboundPhoneNumber` with valid country code and number


### Security and Compliance Considerations[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#security-and-compliance-considerations "Direct link to Security and Compliance Considerations")
  * Consent records should be retained according to NACHA retention requirements (generally 2 years)
  * Sensitive consent information should be properly encrypted in transit and at rest
  * Audit trails should track consent collection and usage throughout the payment lifecycle


## Sample Consent Objects[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/ach/consent/#sample-consent-objects "Direct link to Sample Consent Objects")

# Manufacturer Card
### What is Manufacturer card?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#what-is-manufacturer-card "Direct link to What is Manufacturer card?")
A manufactured card, also known as a copay card or manufacturer-sponsored discount card, is issued by a pharmaceutical manufacturer to help reduce the out-of-pocket cost to support access to high-cost drugs.
They come in different forms but not limited:
  * **Single-use cards** : Valid for a one-time transaction.
  * **Multi-use or recurring cards:** Usable over multiple visits or prescription fills, often subject to predefined limits or expiration periods.


#### Example[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#example "Direct link to Example")
  * **Walgreens Credit Card** (issued by Synchrony Bank, usable only at Walgreens and Duane Reade stores, a chain of pharmacy and convenience stores owned by Walgreens)


## Business Rules[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#business-rules "Direct link to Business Rules")
  * **Category Configuration** : MF cards are recognized as a new category type `MANUFACTURER_CARD`. Refer to [payment method settings](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/).
  * **Usage** : _Adding_ or _making payments_ with MF cards depends on this category configuration. However, _editing_ or _deleting_ MF cards is always allowed.
  * **Medication Link** : Every MF card must be linked to a medication.
  * **Default Restriction** : MF cards cannot be set as the [default](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/default-payment-method/) payment method. [Learn more](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/default-payment-method/#manufacturer-card-cannot-be-designated-as-default)
  * **3DS Exemption** : MF cards are exempt from [3DS authorisation](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/). [Learn more](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/3ds-authentication/#3ds-enabled-card-cannot-be-designated-as-a-manufacturer-card)
  * **Card Validation** : Validation is skipped for single-use MF cards during addition but not during payments.
    * When adding a card, Stripe performs [penny transactions](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/developers/getting-started/stripe/card-validation/#4-zero-value-authorization) for [card validations](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/developers/getting-started/stripe/card-validation/). However: Manufacturer cards _could_ be a single-use card, making penny validation irrelevant. This validation is intentionally skipped by CCG.
    * Some manufacturer card issuers prohibit $0 authorizations (e.g., single-use cards preloaded with $25 may only allow transactions equal to the preloaded amount).


important
  * CCG sets `verify_card_account` to `false` in the `set-up-intent-request` sent to Stripe.
  * Skipping card validation is a gated feature within Stripe.
  * This workaround remains active until Stripe implements a scalable, secure, long-term solution.


## Terminology[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#terminology "Direct link to Terminology")
### Legacy MF Card[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#legacy-mf-card "Direct link to Legacy MF Card")
a MF card not linked with a medication
info
'Legacy' doesn't just imply existing older cards in the system, as **new** legacy MF card can be added to the wallet by legacy client.
### Legacy Client[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#legacy-client "Direct link to Legacy Client")
Refers to an API consumer using the old contract format to manage MF card.
A client is considered legacy if "request payload" includes the `manufacturerCard` flag:
```
// sample req payload (add MF card flow / one time pay flow / pay and save flow)  
  
{  
    "paymentMethod": {  
        "paymentMethodDetails": {  
            "manufacturerCard": true // boolean   
        }  
}  

```

### New Client[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#new-client "Direct link to New Client")
Refers to an API consumer using the new contract format to manage MF card.
A client is considered new if "request payload" includes the `cardCategories` structure:
```
// sample req payload (add MF card flow / one time pay flow / pay and save flow)  
{  
    "paymentMethod": {  
        "paymentMethodDetails": {  
            "cardCategories": {  
                "type": "MANUFACTURER_CARD",  
                "medications": [  
                {  
                  "label": "Tremfya", // string  
                  "value": "5mg" // string  
                }  
              ]  
            }  
        }  
}  

```

### Manufacture Card Category Structure[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#manufacture-card-category-structure "Direct link to Manufacture Card Category Structure")
Field | Type | Valid values | Required | Constraints | Example  
---|---|---|---|---|---  
`type` | Enum | MANUFACTURE_CARD | Yes |  `"MANUFACTURER_CARD"` only | `"MANUFACTURER_CARD"`  
`label` | String |  | Yes | Max 100 chars | `"Pharmacy card"`  
`medications` | Object | [Medication](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#medication-structure) | No | List of `{label, value}` | See below  
### Medication Structure[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#medication-structure "Direct link to Medication Structure")
Field | Type | Required | Example  
---|---|---|---  
`label` | String | Yes | `"Tremfya"`  
`value` | String | Yes | `"10mg"`  
## Constraints[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#constraints "Direct link to Constraints")
  * `type` must be `"MANUFACTURER_CARD"` for manufacturer cards.
  * `label` is required and ≤ 100 characters.
  * `medications` is optional; if present, each must have both `label` and `value`.


## Validation Rules[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#validation-rules "Direct link to Validation Rules")
  * `type` must be a recognized enumeration value (e.g., `MANUFACTURER_CARD`).
  * If `type` is `MANUFACTURER_CARD`, `medications` **must** be present.
  * If `label` is present, it must be a non-empty string; if not provided, it defaults to the merchant-configured value.
  * Each entry in `medications[]` must include:
    * `label`: non-empty string and ≤ 100 characters.
    * `value`: non-empty string and ≤ 100 characters.


## Handling Mixed Payload Formats[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#handling-mixed-payload-formats "Direct link to Handling Mixed Payload Formats")
When a client sends a "request payload" containing both the old (manufacturerCard flag) and new (cardCategories structure) formats, the system will ignore the old format and process the payload using the new format. This ensures consistency with the latest business rules and avoids ambiguity.
```
// sample req payload: (add MF card flow / one time pay flow / pay and save flow)  
{    
    "paymentMethod": {    
        "paymentMethodDetails": {    
            "manufacturerCard": true, // boolean Old format (ignored)    
            "cardCategories": {    
                "type": "MANUFACTURER_CARD",    
                "medications": [    
                    {    
                        "label": "Tremfya", // string  
                        "value": "5mg" // string  
                    }    
                ]    
            }    
        }    
    }    
}    

```

### Use Case Handling Summary[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payment-methods/payment-methods-types/card/manufacturer-card/#use-case-handling-summary "Direct link to Use Case Handling Summary")
Scenario | Merchant Configured with MANUFACTURER_CARD | Merchant Not Configured with MANUFACTURER_CARD  
---|---|---  
`cardCategories` present in session request | Honor `cardCategories` and persist in DB. | Ignore `cardCategories`, save session without it  
cardCategories is not present in session request | Save session request as-is in DB. | Save session request as-is in DB.  
cardCategories is present in session request and no medications | Honor cardCategories and persist and persist without medications in DB. | Ignore cardCategories, save session without it.

# Payment Modes
CCG allows following payment modes
  * Pay with Wallet
  * One Time Pay
  * Pay and Store


## Pay with Wallet[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/payment-modes/#pay-with-wallet "Direct link to Pay with Wallet")
Pay with Wallet refers to making a payment using a digital wallet or mobile wallet application. A digital wallet is a virtual wallet that allows users to securely store payment information, such as credit/debit card details, bank account information, and other payment methods, on a mobile device or online platform.
## One Time Pay[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/payment-modes/#one-time-pay "Direct link to One Time Pay")
One-time payment refers to a single payment made by the payer to resolve a debt, acquire goods or services, or meet a financial obligation. In contrast to recurring payments or subscriptions, a one-time payment does not entail continuous charges or automatic withdrawals from the payer's account. This payment method enables the payer to make a solitary payment for a particular purpose without the requirement for recurring payments or sustained financial obligations
## Pay and Save[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/payment-modes/#pay-and-save "Direct link to Pay and Save")
Pay and Save is crucial for managing subscriptions, installment payments, and recurring expenses, as it involves setting up automatic deductions from the individual's account at regular intervals, such as monthly or annually. By incorporating a savings component, Pay and Save enables individuals to streamline financial management, automate the savings process, and make significant strides towards securing a stable financial future.
## IVR[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/payment-modes/#ivr "Direct link to IVR")
IVR stands for Interactive Voice Response. It is a technology that allows automated interactions with callers through voice and touch-tone inputs. IVR systems can provide information, route calls, and enable self-service options without the need for human intervention
IVR technology is commonly used in payment gateways for various purposes, including:
  * **Payment Processing** : IVR systems can securely process payments over the phone by allowing customers to enter their payment information using their touch-tone keypad.
  * **Payment Verification** : IVR can be used to verify payment details, such as confirming payment amounts, transaction IDs, or account numbers.
  * **Payment Reminders** : IVR can send automated payment reminders to customers, prompting them to make payments or update their payment information.
  * **Customer Service** : IVR systems can handle customer inquiries related to payments, account balances, transaction history, and more, providing a self-service option for customers.
  * **Payment Authentication** : IVR can be used for two-factor authentication or verification purposes to ensure secure payment transactions.




# Disputes
## Overview[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/disputes/#overview "Direct link to Overview")
If a dispute occurs on one card within a split tender transaction, how should disputes and related webhooks be managed?
## Recommended Approach[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/disputes/#recommended-approach "Direct link to Recommended Approach")
  * Handle disputes independently for each payment method while maintaining a reference to the original split tender transaction
  * Webhook Handling: Each dispute webhook should reference both the individual payment ID and the parent transaction ID
  * Merchant Notification: Provide clear indication to the merchant that the dispute affects only part of a split tender transaction


## Current Implementation[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/disputes/#current-implementation "Direct link to Current Implementation")
### Dispute Resolution[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/disputes/#dispute-resolution "Direct link to Dispute Resolution")
  * If a dispute is WON, a dispute event will be sent to the merchant with the merchant transaction ID
  * The payment status in Convenient Checkout Gateway (CCG) will not be reversed
  * Refer [Dispute Webhooks](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/v1/developers/add-on-services/webhooks/disputes/) for additional information


### Impact on Split Tender Transactions[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/disputes/#impact-on-split-tender-transactions "Direct link to Impact on Split Tender Transactions")
When a dispute occurs on one payment method within a split tender transaction:
  * Only the disputed portion of the transaction is affected
  * Other payment methods used in the same transaction remain unaffected
  * The merchant can identify which specific payment method was disputed through the payment ID reference




# Refunds
## What is a Refund?[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#what-is-a-refund "Direct link to What is a Refund?")
A refund is the return of funds to a customer after they have made a payment for a product or service. Refunds are typically issued when a customer is dissatisfied with a product or service, when an error occurs in the transaction, or when a business policy allows for returns.
## Types of Refunds[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#types-of-refunds "Direct link to Types of Refunds")
### Linked Refund[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#linked-refund "Direct link to Linked Refund")
Linked refunds are processed against an existing completed payment transaction. A successfully completed transaction is required before a linked refund can be issued.
### Unlinked Refund[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#unlinked-refund "Direct link to Unlinked Refund")
An unlinked refund (also known as a credit or cashback) is issued directly to the payment method ID without requiring a prior transaction. This allows for issuing credits to customers without an original transaction reference.
## Business Rules[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#business-rules "Direct link to Business Rules")
### Pre-Conditions for All Refunds[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#pre-conditions-for-all-refunds "Direct link to Pre-Conditions for All Refunds")
  * A valid refund reason must be provided. Acceptable reasons are:
    * `REQUESTED_BY_CUSTOMER`
    * `DUPLICATE`
    * `FRAUDULENT`
  * A unique `MerchantTransactionId` is required to issue any refund


### Linked Refund Requirements[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#linked-refund-requirements "Direct link to Linked Refund Requirements")
  * The original payment transaction must have a status of `COMPLETED`
  * Refund amount must be less than or equal to the original payment amount
  * If no amount is specified, the full original payment amount will be refunded
  * The following refund types are supported:
    * **Partial Refunds** : Only a portion of the transaction amount is refunded
    * **Full Refunds** : The entire transaction amount is refunded
    * **Multiple Refunds** : Multiple partial refunds can be processed for a single transaction, but the cumulative refund amount cannot exceed the total transaction amount


### Unlinked Refund Requirements[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#unlinked-refund-requirements "Direct link to Unlinked Refund Requirements")
  * Valid customer and payment method is required
  * Specific refund amount must be provided
  * Bank account payment method are not supported for unlinked refunds
  * Partial & Full Refunds are not applicable for Unlinked Refunds


## Refund Statuses[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#refund-statuses "Direct link to Refund Statuses")
Refunds may transition through the following statuses:
  * `PENDING`: The refund request has been received and is being processed
  * `COMPLETED`: The refund has been successfully processed and funds are being returned to the customer
  * `FAILED`: The refund could not be processed due to an error or validation failure


## Business Use Case Flows[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/refunds/#business-use-case-flows "Direct link to Business Use Case Flows")

When a refund is processed, notifications may be sent to:

# Split Tender Cancellation
Quick Reference
  * **Purpose:** Understand CCG's handling of cancellation requests for split tender payments.
  * **Key Scenarios:** Complete cancellation, handling of cancellation failures, and retry strategies.
  * **Use:** Refer to the table for status mapping and outcome summaries for different cancellation scenarios.


* * *
## CCG Split Payments Cancel Process[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/cancel/#ccg-split-payments-cancel-process "Direct link to CCG Split Payments Cancel Process")
The diagram above illustrates how CCG orchestrates split tender cancellation requests:
  1. **Cancellation Request** : CCG receives a request to cancel authorized split tender payments
  2. **Orchestrated Cancellation** : CCG attempts to cancel both payments in the split tender transaction
  3. **Outcome Handling** :
     * For successful cancellations of both payments, status is CANCELLED
     * For temporary failures due to 5XX errors, CCG automatically retries the cancellation
     * For permanent failures on one payment, a PARTIAL_CANCELLED status is returned
  4. **Merchant Decision Point** : When one payment cancellation fails permanently, merchants may need to decide whether to retry the cancellation manually


This approach ensures that split tender cancellations are handled with appropriate recovery mechanisms while providing clear status information for exception cases.
* * *
## Key Split Tender Cancellation Scenarios[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/cancel/#key-split-tender-cancellation-scenarios "Direct link to Key Split Tender Cancellation Scenarios")
Scenario | Description | Final Outcome  
---|---|---  
1 |  **Full Cancellation** : Both payments cancelled successfully | CANCELLED  
2 |  **Cancellation with Retry** : One payment cancellation fails with 5XX error - CCG retries | CANCELLED after retry  
3 |  **Permanent Cancellation Failure** : One payment cancellation fails permanently | PARTIAL_CANCELLED (merchant decision required)  
* * *

# Sessions (Split Tender via UI)
Split tender transactions allow customers to pay for a single order using up to two payment methods in a single session. This approach increases payment flexibility, reduces cart abandonment, and supports scenarios where a single payment method is insufficient.
Scope
  * **Session Mode:** `PAYMENT_WITH_WALLET` **|** **API Scope:** `user` **|** **API Endpoint:** `v2/sessions` **|** **Interaction mode:** `UI`
  * **Maximum number of payment methods:** 2
  * **Payment Type:** `SALE`
  * **Transaction Type:** Any


Out-Of-Scope
  * **Mode:** `One Time Pay` `Pay & Save`
  * **Payment Type:** `PRE-AUTH`


## Transaction Processing[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/business-use-case/sale/ui/#transaction-processing "Direct link to Transaction Processing")
For UI-based split tender transactions using the Sessions API, the system processes payments in parallel:
  1. **Payment Methods Selection:** Customer selects both payment methods and allocates amounts (in cents) to each.
  2. **Parallel Processing:** Both payment methods are processed simultaneously for faster response time.
  3. **Transaction Result:** System combines both payments and provides a unified result to the customer and merchant.


Parallel Processing
Payment methods in split tender transactions are processed in parallel to optimize transaction processing time and provide a faster checkout experience for customers. If either payment fails, the entire transaction is considered failed and any successful payment is reversed.
Process Flow
**UI Session Split Tender Process Flow**
Payment Method 2Payment Method 1CCGUICustomerPayment Method 2Payment Method 1CCGUICustomer par[Parallel Processing]alt[Both Payments Successful][One or More Payments ❌ FAILED]Initiates checkoutCreate SessionSession createdDisplay payment optionsSelect payment methodsAllocate amounts to each methodSubmit payment requestProcess first paymentProcess second paymentPayment 1 resultPayment 2 resultSplit payment successfulDisplay success messageReverse successful payment(s)Split payment failedDisplay error and retry options
### User Experience Flow[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/business-use-case/sale/ui/#user-experience-flow "Direct link to User Experience Flow")
  1. **Initial Payment Screen:** Customer sees saved payment methods and total due (in cents).
  2. **Payment Methods Selection:** Customer selects both payment methods and allocates amounts (must be ≥ 1¢ each).
  3. **Review and Confirm:** Customer reviews split and confirms.
  4. **Parallel Processing:** Both payments are processed at the same time.
  5. **Completion:** On success, customer is redirected to the merchant's return URL. On failure, clear error and retry options are shown.


UI Validation
  * **Amount Limitation**
    * Split Tender should not be allowed when amount specified less than 2 cents at parent level
    * Amount should not be allowed to be less than 1 cent at each payment level under split tender transaction
  * **ACH Payment**
    * If Consent is unavailable, UI should restrict ACH payment
    * Bank accounts cannot be selected for split tender transactions when PRE-AUTH is the payment type, as ACH payments only support sale transactions.


Session Management
**Session States for Split Tender Transactions**
  * `CREATED`: Initial state after session creation
  * `INITIATED`: Consumer has started the payment process
  * `✅ COMPLETED`: When payment is ✅ COMPLETED
  * `CANCELLED`: When session is cancelled
  * `EXPIRED`: When session is expired
  * `❌ FAILED`: Payment method Error


3DS Authentication
**3DS Authentication requirements for Card split transactions**
  * 3D Secure authentication may be required for either card based on the issuing bank's risk assessment
  * When 3DS is triggered for either card, the authentication will proceed independently
  * Both cards' 3DS authentications can occur simultaneously if needed
  * Failed 3DS authentication on either card will result in the entire transaction being declined
  * For international cards, 3DS requirements may differ based on regional regulations
  * If 3DS authentication times out, the system will consider it a failed authentication
  * Merchants can configure whether to require 3DS based on transaction risk profiles




# Split Tender Capture
Quick Reference
  * **Purpose:** Understand CCG's handling of capture requests for split tender payments.
  * **Key Scenarios:** Complete capture, partial capture, and handling of capture failures.
  * **Use:** Refer to the table for status mapping and outcome summaries for different capture scenarios.


## CCG Split Payment Capture Process[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/capture/#ccg-split-payment-capture-process "Direct link to CCG Split Payment Capture Process")
The diagram above illustrates how CCG orchestrates split tender capture requests:
  1. **Capture Request** : Merchant initiates a capture request for authorized split tender payments
  2. **Request Types** :
     * Complete capture of both payments
     * Capture of only one payment (with automatic cancellation of the other)
     * Partial amount capture of both payments
  3. **Outcome Handling** :
     * For successful captures of both payments, status is COMPLETED
     * For temporary failures, CCG retries the capture
     * For permanent failures on one payment, a PARTIAL_SUCCESS status is returned
  4. **Merchant Decision Point** : When one payment capture fails permanently, merchants must decide whether to refund the successful payment


This approach ensures that split tender captures are handled with appropriate atomicity while providing flexibility for partial capture scenarios.
* * *
## Key Split Tender Capture Scenarios[​](https://developers.healthsafepay.com/docs/business/core-capabilities/payments/split-tender/capture/#key-split-tender-capture-scenarios "Direct link to Key Split Tender Capture Scenarios")
Scenario | Description | Final Outcome  
---|---|---  
1 |  **Full Capture** : Both payments captured successfully | COMPLETED  
2 |  **Single Payment Capture** : Only one payment captured, other cancelled | COMPLETED  
3 |  **Partial Amount Capture** : Both payments captured with partial amounts | COMPLETED  
4 |  **Capture Retry** : One payment capture fails with 5XX error - CCG retries | COMPLETED after retry  
5 |  **Permanent Capture Failure** : One payment capture fails permanently | PARTIAL_SUCCESS (merchant decision required)  
* * *
